about: Which customers, leads and routes a rep may see. Both apps read this file in their tests. The rule exists because the UAE unit works differently from the Indian ones: four reps and a manager cover for each other's leave, so any of them must be able to serve any UAE customer. Everywhere else a rep sees only their own.

fields.note: Pooling widens VISIBILITY only. Every customer, lead and route still names one owner, because the business still needs to know whose it is - for the route plan, for accountability, and to show who is being covered for.

visible.why: a UAE rep sees every UAE rep's customers, because any of them may have to cover a colleague's leave at no notice - this is the whole reason the rule exists
the UAE manager is in the pool like everyone else - he carries his own customers and covers too
an Indian rep sees ONLY their own, unchanged - pooling one unit must not quietly widen the others
a rep on the other Indian team is likewise untouched
a disabled rep is not in the pool - somebody who has left must not keep appearing as a person on cover
a group node is not a person and never appears
a login that matches no Sales Person sees NOTHING - failing closed, because the alternative is showing one unit's customers to another
a rep with no unit recorded sees only their own, never the pool - missing data must not be read as membership

pooled.why: an unknown unit is not pooled - a new unit must be opted in deliberately, never by default
no unit at all is not pooled
